Alias for a pointer-to-member function type denoting a cpr::Session method that takes no arguments and returns cpr::Response (e.g., &cpr::Session::Get). Used by templated helpers to schedule multiple asynchronous operations.

Alias for an asynchronous response handle produced by wrapper utilities around cpr::Response. It represents the result type returned by the async request methods (e.g., GetAsync). The underlying type is AsyncWrapper<Response>.
Alias representing the request body/content variant used internally by Session. It may hold nothing (monostate), a Payload, Body, BodyView, or Multipart.
Forward declaration of an interceptor interface/class used to hook into the request pipeline. Definition is not present in this header; details unknown.
Forward declaration of a helper managing multi-request execution (likely libcurl multi interface). Definition is not present in this header; details unknown.

HTTP client session object managing request configuration, execution, and callbacks. Not copyable/movable; meant to be managed via std::shared_ptr (inherits enable_shared_from_this). Provides synchronous and asynchronous request APIs, supports interceptors, and stores internal state like headers, proxies, and body content.
Forward declaration of a class used as a friend of cpr::Response. No fields or methods are defined here; it is an incomplete type in this header.

Concrete HTTP response object for the cpr library. Holds status code, body text, headers, URL, timing, cookies, error info, raw header/status line, reason phrase, byte counters, redirect count, and connection endpoint. Internally keeps a shared_ptr to a CurlHolder for libcurl details and grants friendship to MultiPerform. Provides default/copy/move constructors and assignment, a value-initializing constructor that accepts curl handle plus response components, and a method to extract certificate info. Construction/destruction specifics beyond defaults are not documented here.

A singleton thread pool class in namespace cpr deriving from ThreadPool. It exposes a singleton interface via CPR_SINGLETON_DECL(GlobalThreadPool) macro (definition not shown here) and uses defaulted constructor/destructor. Likely manages a global pool used by async task submission in this header.
Strongly-typed enum indicating the outcome of attempting to cancel an async operation: failure, success, or invalid_operation (e.g., already cancelled or invalid future).
Strongly scoped enumeration specifying the HTTP authentication scheme to use (basic, digest, NTLM, negotiate, or auto-select modes ANY/ANYSAFE).

Encapsulates credentials and selected AuthMode for HTTP authentication. Stores an internal secure string representation and exposes it via GetAuthString along with the chosen mode. Construction requires username, password, and an AuthMode. Details of the secure storage and formatting are defined elsewhere.

Bearer is a small RAII value class in namespace cpr that holds a bearer-token string for HTTP Authorization headers when libcurl >= 7.61.0 is available. It stores the token in a util::SecureString and exposes it via GetToken() as a C string. Copyable and movable; destructor is noexcept and virtual. Construction takes a std::string_view token. No ownership relationships are implied beyond holding the secure string. If LIBCURL_VERSION_NUM is below 0x073D00, this class is not defined in the translation unit.

HTTP request body wrapper in namespace cpr. Inherits from StringHolder<Body> (defined elsewhere) to manage an internal string (likely str_) representing the payload. Provides multiple constructors to build a body from std::string, std::string_view, C-strings (with or without length), initializer_list of strings, a Buffer, or a File (reads entire file into memory). Copy/move/assign and virtual destructor are defaulted. Unknown details of StringHolder and internal storage beyond inferred string behavior.

Lightweight non-owning view of an HTTP request body in the cpr namespace. It wraps a std::string_view over external character data and provides implicit construction from std::string_view, C strings (with or without explicit length), and from cpr::Buffer. It does not own or manage lifetime of the underlying data; callers must ensure the referenced memory outlives the BodyView usage.

Contiguous byte-buffer view and associated filename used by cpr. Holds a pointer to the first byte (const char*), the byte length, and an immutable filesystem path. Constructed from a random-access byte iterator range and a filename path; enforces that the iterator is random-access and value size is 1 byte. The constructor stores a pointer to the underlying data via reinterpret_cast and records the size with std::distance. Note: lifetime of the pointed-to data must outlive the Buffer; it does not own the memory. Filename is stored by move and is const thereafter.

Functor class that supplies data to an HTTP request body reader. Invokes a user-provided function to fill a buffer, optionally with a known total size via size field. If callback is empty, operator() returns true (no-op/continue). Requires cpr_off_t from cprtypes.h.
Functor to process HTTP header lines as they are received. Calls a user-provided function with each header line and userdata. If no callback is set, operator() returns true to continue.
Functor to consume response body data chunks. Invokes a user callback with the received data and userdata. If callback is empty, operator() returns true to continue.

Functor for transfer progress reporting. Calls user function with totals and current counts for download and upload, plus userdata. Returning false can be used to cancel transfers depending on caller. Types cpr_pf_arg_t come from cprtypes.h.

Functor for debug logging/tracing during transfers. Accepts an InfoType indicating what kind of information is provided (text, headers, data, SSL data) and the data payload. Invokes user callback with userdata. Includes nested scoped enum InfoType.
Scoped enum nested in cpr::DebugCallback describing debug information categories: text, incoming/outgoing headers, incoming/outgoing data, and SSL-specific data directions.

Functor that wraps a progress callback with a cancellation mechanism. Holds a shared atomic_bool state to indicate cancellation and optionally forwards progress to a user-supplied ProgressCallback. operator() and SetProgressCallback are declared here but defined elsewhere.

Container class in namespace cpr that wraps a std::vector<std::string> representing certificate information entries. Provides vector-like iteration, element access, and modifiers. Constructors include default, copy, move, and initialization from an initializer_list of strings. Destructor is noexcept and defaulted. Details of semantics beyond storing strings are not documented in this header.

Concrete timeout type in the cpr namespace representing the timeout for establishing a connection. It derives from Timeout (declared in cpr/timeout.h) and provides two convenience constructors that forward to the base Timeout: one from std::chrono::milliseconds and one from a 32-bit integer value representing milliseconds. No additional state beyond the base is added.

A pool object that enables libcurl connection reuse across multiple HTTP requests using a shared CURLSH handle and a mutex for thread-safe locking. Constructed via its public default constructor; copy-constructible to share the same underlying shared state; copy assignment is disabled. Call SetupHandler on a CURL easy handle to attach it to the pool. Internally owns a shared_ptr to a mutex used by libcurl lock callbacks and a shared_ptr to a CURLSH handle with a custom deleter. Destruction order is arranged so the CURLSH is cleaned up before the mutex. Exact custom deleter details are not visible in this header.

Represents a single HTTP cookie with name, value, domain, path, HTTPS-only flag, subdomain inclusion, and expiration time. Provides accessors and a constructor to initialize fields. Implementation details of methods are not present in this header.

Container and helper for multiple cpr::Cookie values. Tracks whether cookies should be URL-encoded when building request headers. Provides vector-like interface, index operator, and an encoding method that depends on CurlHolder. Method implementations are not in this header.

Simple key/value pair structure intended for HTTP-style parameters. Holds two strings: key and value. Constructible from two std::string values; movable due to use of std::move in the constructor. No ownership or special lifecycle beyond standard struct semantics is implied.

Generic key/value pair structure holding two strings. Similar to cpr::Parameter but named Pair, likely used for headers or other name/value contexts. Constructible from two std::string values; move-friendly.

RAII-style holder around a libcurl easy handle and related resources for a single request. Manages CURL* handle, header list (chunk), resolve list, mime multipart, and an error buffer. Provides URL encode/decode helpers that delegate to curl_easy_escape/unescape. Construction/destruction details are not fully visible here; assume constructor initializes libcurl handle and destructor frees associated libcurl resources. Thread-safety note: a private static mutex accessor is provided to guard curl_easy_init to avoid non-thread-safe initialization issues.

RAII-style holder class in namespace cpr that owns a libcurl multi handle (CURLM*). namespace cpr {
enum class HttpVersionCode {
    /**
     * Let libcurl decide which version is the best.
     **/
    VERSION_NONE,
    /**
     * Enforce HTTP 1.0 requests.
     **/
    VERSION_1_0,
    /**
     * Enforce HTTP 1.1 requests.
     **/
    VERSION_1_1,
#if LIBCURL_VERSION_NUM >= 0x072100 // 7.33.0
    /**
     * Attempt HTTP 2.0 requests.
     * Fallback to HTTP 1.1 if negotiation fails.
     **/
    VERSION_2_0,
#endif
#if LIBCURL_VERSION_NUM >= 0x072F00 // 7.47.0
    /**
     * Attempt HTTP 2.0 for HTTPS requests only.
     * Fallback to HTTP 1.1 if negotiation fails.
     * HTTP 1.1 will be used for HTTP connections.
     **/
    VERSION_2_0_TLS,
#endif
#if LIBCURL_VERSION_NUM >= 0x073100 // 7.49.0
    /**
     * Start HTTP 2.0 for HTTP requests.
     * Requires prior knowledge that the server supports HTTP 2.0.
     * For HTTPS requests we will negotiate the protocol version in the TLS handshake.
     **/
    VERSION_2_0_PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE,
#endif
#if LIBCURL_VERSION_NUM >= 0x074200 // 7.66.0
    /**
     * Attempt HTTP 3.0 requests.
     * Requires prior knowledge that the server supports HTTP 3.0 since there is no gracefully downgrade.
     * Fallback to HTTP 1.1 if negotiation fails.
     **/
    VERSION_3_0,
#endif
#if LIBCURL_VERSION_NUM >= 0x075701 // 7.87.1, but corresponds to 7.88.0 tag
    /**
     * Enforce HTTP 3.0 requests without fallback.
     * Requires prior knowledge that the server supports HTTP 3.0 since there is no gracefully downgrade.
     **/
    VERSION_3_0_ONLY
#endif
};
}
objects.description: Strongly-typed enumeration of HTTP protocol version policies for cpr/libcurl. Values map to desired version behavior (HTTP/1.0, 1.1, 2.0 modes, and 3.0 modes) with availability gated by the detected libcurl version. Used to tell libcurl which HTTP version to negotiate or enforce.

Lightweight value-holder class encapsulating a desired HTTP version policy for cpr/libcurl via its public member `code` of type HttpVersionCode. Default constructs to VERSION_NONE (let libcurl decide) or can be explicitly constructed from a specific HttpVersionCode.

Abstract base class in cpr for single-request interception. Implementations override intercept(Session&) to observe/modify a Session before delegating to one of the protected static proceed(...) helpers that actually performs the HTTP operation, optionally specifying an HTTP method or download target/callback. Used to build middleware such as logging, retry, auth, or request mutation. Details of Response, Session, and WriteCallback are defined elsewhere.

A lightweight string wrapper type in the cpr namespace representing a network interface identifier (e.g., OS network interface name). It derives from StringHolder<Interface> (defined elsewhere) to provide value semantics and implicit construction from various string forms. No additional members beyond those provided by the base; lifecycle is defaulted. Details of storage/validation come from StringHolder.

A simple rate-limiting value holder in the cpr namespace that stores download and upload rate limits as 64-bit signed integers. It provides a constructor to set both limits and exposes the fields publicly. No custom destructor or special ownership semantics are defined; it is a trivial class used to pass or hold rate-limit configuration. Construction: use the provided constructor with desired downrate and uprate values. Destruction: default. Thread-safety or units are not specified in this header.

Lightweight value-type wrapper around a 16-bit unsigned integer representing a local TCP/UDP port. Provides implicit conversion to std::uint16_t for convenient API use. Stores the port number in a private member and offers no additional behavior beyond construction and conversion.

A lightweight value-wrapper class in the cpr namespace that stores a 16-bit integer representing a local port range setting and allows implicit conversion to std::uint16_t. Primarily used to pass a strongly-typed option into APIs expecting a port range value. No dynamic resources; trivially copyable and assignable by default. Construction requires a 16-bit value; it converts back to uint16_t via the conversion operator.

A small value-type class in the cpr namespace representing a low-speed condition: if transfer speed stays below `limit` (bytes/second) for a duration `time`, an operation may be treated as too slow. Provides two constructors: a deprecated one taking an int32 time (converted to seconds) and the preferred one taking std::chrono::seconds. Public fields expose the threshold and duration directly. No ownership semantics or special destruction behavior beyond default.

Multipart form-data element that can represent a simple text field, a set of files, or an in-memory buffer. Flags is_file and is_buffer indicate which variant is active; when both are false, the part is a text field using name/value. When is_file is true, files holds the file attachments. When is_buffer is true, data/datalen hold the payload and value holds a filename string for the buffer. content_type can override the default MIME type.

Container for a set of multipart form-data parts. Provides constructors from initializer_list and vectors of Part to assemble multipart payloads for HTTP requests. Owns its Part elements via the parts vector.

Orchestrator class in namespace cpr that performs multiple HTTP requests concurrently using a Curl multi handle. It manages a vector of Session/method pairs, prepares requests (including downloads), supports an interceptor chain, and exposes operations such as Get/Post/Delete/Perform. Copy is disabled; move is allowed. Destruction likely cleans up the underlying CurlMultiHolder. Details of Session, Response, CurlMultiHolder, InterceptorMulti, WriteCallback, and CURLcode are referenced but defined elsewhere.

A thin container class in the cpr namespace that aggregates Parameter items by inheriting from CurlContainer<Parameter>. It provides a default constructor and a convenience constructor from an initializer_list of Parameter. Details of storage, lifetime, and behavior are defined by CurlContainer; Parameter and CurlContainer are referenced but not defined in this header. Destruction and copying semantics follow those of the base class. Unknown details: memory ownership model and thread-safety, as they depend on CurlContainer.

A lightweight container class in the cpr namespace that aggregates key/value Pair items for HTTP payloads. It derives from CurlContainer<Pair>, inheriting storage and Add behavior. It provides two constructors: one templated range constructor that iterates [begin, end) and adds each Pair via Add, and one that forwards an initializer_list<Pair> to the base class. No other behavior or ownership beyond what is provided by CurlContainer is defined here. Details about Pair and CurlContainer are external to this header.

A small map-like helper class in namespace cpr that stores proxy settings, mapping protocol names (e.g., "http", "https") to proxy host strings. It provides default and convenience constructors from an initializer_list and std::map, a query to check for a protocol, and a non-const operator[] accessor. Internal storage is a std::map<string,string>. Destruction/ownership is automatic; no special lifetime rules are indicated. Exact semantics of operator[] (e.g., insertion on miss) and has() are not documented here and would depend on the implementation in the source file.

Holds a URL-encoded username and password for proxy authentication. It stores credentials in util::SecureString and exposes string_view accessors as well as access to the underlying secure strings. Construction from username/password encodes them via util::urlEncode. Copy/move/default construction and assignment are supported; destructor is noexcept. Details of util::SecureString and util::urlEncode are external to this header.

Container mapping protocol strings (e.g., "http", "https") to EncodedAuthentication credentials for use with proxies. Provides constructors from initializer_list and std::map, plus query and accessor methods by protocol. Owns EncodedAuthentication instances in an internal std::map.

Represents a byte range with optional start (resume_from) and end (finish_at) offsets, suitable for HTTP Range headers. Negative values indicate an unspecified boundary when rendering via str(). Default constructor semantics: start defaults to 0 and end defaults to -1 (unspecified).
Container for multiple cpr::Range values, rendering as a comma-separated list suitable for an HTTP Range header with multiple segments.

Strongly-typed bitflag enum controlling how POST requests behave after HTTP redirects. Flags correspond to libcurl POST redirect semantics (301/302/303). Intended to be combined via the provided bitwise helpers to configure Redirect::post_flags.

Configuration object for HTTP redirect behavior in cpr. Holds maximum redirect count, whether to follow redirects, whether to continue sending credentials across redirects, and POST redirect handling flags. Provides multiple convenience constructors.

Small utility/value class in the cpr namespace that holds a single size_t indicating a desired reservation size (likely for pre-allocating buffers or containers). It has a single explicit-like constructor taking the target size and a public member "size" initialized to 0 by default. No destructor or special semantics are defined.

Concrete class representing a DNS resolution specification within the cpr namespace. It stores a host name, a resolved address string, and a set of TCP ports. The constructor initializes fields and ensures the ports set is never empty by defaulting to {80, 443} if not provided or if an empty set is passed. No destructor or special ownership semantics are defined; members are standard library types. Copy/move semantics are implicitly defaulted. Usage: create with host and address, optionally providing ports.

Provides Milliseconds() to retrieve the timeout as a long, matching libcurl expectations. The public member ms holds the value; no destructor or special ownership semantics are defined.

A small value-semantic wrapper class in namespace cpr representing an HTTP User-Agent header value. It derives from StringHolder<UserAgent> (defined elsewhere) to store and manage the underlying string and provide convenient implicit construction from std::string, std::string_view, const char*, length pairs, and initializer_list of strings. It supports copy/move construction and assignment, and has a virtual destructor overriding the base. Details of storage, formatting, and validation come from StringHolder; those specifics are not visible in this header.

It stores a single boolean flag, defaulting to true, and offers a default constructor and a converting constructor from bool. No destructor or special management semantics are defined.

The memory in the range [begin, end) must be contiguous, as the implementation stores &(*begin) and a byte length for later use.
The underlying storage for [begin, end) must outlive the cpr::Buffer’s usage since the data pointer is non-owning and no copy is made.

functions.name: cpr::Error::operator bool

requirements: The cpr::Files object must outlive any iterator obtained.

functions.name: cpr::Files::end
functions.description: Returns a const iterator one past the last element of the collection. Iteration is read-only.
requirements: The cpr::Files object must outlive any iterator obtained.

Modifying the container may invalidate iterators, including the end iterator.

Marked [[nodiscard]]: callers should use the returned iterator or explicitly discard to avoid warnings.
Modifying the container may invalidate iterators.

functions.name: cpr::Files::cend

functions.name: cpr::Interceptor::Interceptor
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract base class cpr::Interceptor. Intended to be invoked implicitly by derived interceptor classes during construction. The class cannot be instantiated directly because it declares a pure virtual intercept().

Because cpr::Interceptor is abstract, copying occurs only as part of copying a concrete derived class.

functions.name: cpr::Interceptor::Interceptor
functions.description: Move constructor for the abstract base class cpr::Interceptor. Used when moving a derived interceptor object’s base subobject. The class remains abstract and cannot be moved as a standalone instance.
requirements: The source object old must be a valid, fully constructed cpr::Interceptor subobject (typically part of a derived type).
Because cpr::Interceptor is abstract, moving occurs only as part of moving a concrete derived class.

functions.name: cpr::Interceptor::~Interceptor
functions.description: Virtual destructor for cpr::Interceptor, ensuring proper cleanup via base pointers. Enables safe deletion of derived interceptors through a cpr::Interceptor pointer or reference.
requirements: Object must be fully constructed before destruction; delete through a base pointer is safe due to virtual destructor.
No additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: cpr::Interceptor::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator for the cpr::Interceptor base subobject. Typically invoked by a derived class’s copy assignment to copy the base portion. The base class is abstract and not meant to be assigned as a standalone object.

Assigning through a base object slices to the base subobject; use within a derived class’s assignment operator to preserve derived state.

functions.name: cpr::Interceptor::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator for the cpr::Interceptor base subobject. Typically invoked by a derived class’s move assignment to move the base portion. The base class is abstract and not meant to be assigned as a standalone object.
requirements: Both *this and old must be fully constructed cpr::Interceptor subobjects (usually parts of the same concrete derived type).
Assigning through a base object slices to the base subobject; use within a derived class’s move assignment operator to preserve derived state.

functions.name: cpr::Interceptor::intercept
functions.description: Pure virtual hook to intercept and potentially modify or handle a single cpr::Session request. Implementations typically inspect or mutate the session (headers, body, method) and then either perform the request (commonly via protected proceed helpers) or short-circuit by returning a Response directly.
requirements: Must be implemented by concrete derived classes; cpr::Interceptor cannot be instantiated without an implementation.
Parameter session must refer to a valid, initialized cpr::Session that remains alive for the duration of the call.
Return a cpr::Response for every call; if performing the request, derived classes typically call one of the protected proceed(...) overloads (inferred from API design).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; callers should not assume they are thread-safe (unknown).

functions.name: cpr::InterceptorMulti::InterceptorMulti
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract base class cpr::InterceptorMulti. Intended for use by derived multi-interceptor classes during construction. The class cannot be instantiated directly because it declares a pure virtual intercept().

Because cpr::InterceptorMulti is abstract, copying occurs only as part of copying a concrete derived class.

Because cpr::InterceptorMulti is abstract, moving occurs only as part of moving a concrete derived class.

functions.name: cpr::InterceptorMulti::~InterceptorMulti
functions.description: Virtual destructor for cpr::InterceptorMulti, ensuring proper cleanup via base pointers for multi-request interceptors.
requirements: Object must be fully constructed before destruction; deletion through a base pointer is safe due to virtual destructor.
No additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: cpr::InterceptorMulti::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator for the cpr::InterceptorMulti base subobject. Typically invoked by a derived class’s copy assignment.
requirements: Both *this and other must be fully constructed cpr::InterceptorMulti subobjects (usually parts of the same concrete derived type).
Assigning through a base object slices to the base subobject; use within a derived class’s assignment operator to preserve derived state.

functions.name: cpr::InterceptorMulti::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator for the cpr::InterceptorMulti base subobject. Typically invoked by a derived class’s move assignment.
requirements: Both *this and old must be fully constructed cpr::InterceptorMulti subobjects (usually parts of the same concrete derived type).
Assigning through a base object slices to the base subobject; use within a derived class’s move assignment operator to preserve derived state.

functions.name: cpr::InterceptorMulti::intercept
functions.description: Pure virtual hook to intercept and potentially modify or handle a batch of requests represented by cpr::MultiPerform. Implementations typically prepare sessions within the multi, then either execute them (using the protected proceed helper) or short-circuit by producing responses.
requirements: Must be implemented by concrete derived classes; cpr::InterceptorMulti cannot be instantiated without an implementation.
Parameter multi must refer to a valid, initialized cpr::MultiPerform that remains alive for the duration of the call.
Return a vector of cpr::Response for every call; if performing the requests, derived classes typically call the protected proceed(MultiPerform&) helper (inferred from API design).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; callers should not assume they are thread-safe (unknown).

functions.name: cpr::Interface::Interface
functions.description: Default-constructs an Interface option. Intended to represent an empty/unspecified network interface setting for use with CPR requests. Actual semantics depend on how StringHolder<Interface> is interpreted by the library.
requirements: No arguments required.
Resulting object is default-initialized; behavior of an empty Interface value is library-defined and not documented here.

functions.name: cpr::Interface::~Interface
functions.description: Destroys the Interface object. Defaulted and marked override due to inheriting a virtual destructor from StringHolder. No special cleanup beyond what StringHolder performs.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: cpr::Interface::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from another Interface, transferring ownership/state without throwing.
requirements: Assigning to self is permitted; result is the moved-from object left in a valid but unspecified state.
Target object remains valid after assignment; any prior held state is released per StringHolder semantics.

functions.name: cpr::LimitRate::LimitRate
functions.signature: cpr::LimitRate::LimitRate(const std::int64_t p_downrate, const std::int64_t p_uprate)
functions.description: Constructor for cpr::LimitRate that initializes the download and upload rate limits. It stores the provided values into the downrate and uprate members respectively. Intended to be used as a configuration object to carry rate limits; exact units (e.g., bytes/sec) and semantics are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: p_downrate must be a value representable by std::int64_t.
p_uprate must be a value representable by std::int64_t.
No explicit constraints on sign, range, or units are documented in this header; callers should consult higher-level library documentation for semantic requirements.
Object construction has no documented side effects beyond member initialization.

functions.name: cpr::LocalPort::LocalPort
functions.description: Constructs a LocalPort wrapper holding the specified 16-bit local port number. Intended to be passed to cpr APIs that accept a LocalPort; the constructor is intentionally non-explicit to allow implicit construction from a std::uint16_t.
requirements: Argument p_localport is a 16-bit unsigned integer (0..65535) by type.
No additional initialization or setup is required; the constructor simply stores the provided value.
Be aware this constructor is non-explicit, so implicit conversions from std::uint16_t to cpr::LocalPort can occur in overload resolution.

functions.name: cpr::LocalPort::operator std::uint16_t
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator that returns the stored 16-bit port number. Use when a raw std::uint16_t port value is needed from a LocalPort instance.
requirements: Must be called on a valid cpr::LocalPort instance (i.e., constructed).
No side effects; safe to call repeatedly. Returns the stored port value as std::uint16_t.

functions.name: cpr::LocalPortRange::LocalPortRange
functions.description: Constructs a LocalPortRange wrapper holding the provided 16-bit value that represents a local port range. Intended for use as a lightweight option/parameter object; behavior beyond storing the value is not defined in this header.
requirements: Argument p_localportrange is a 16-bit unsigned integer (std::uint16_t).
No validation is performed by this constructor; callers are responsible for providing a semantically valid value for their use case.
Object is initialized to hold exactly the provided value.

functions.name: cpr::LocalPortRange::operator std::uint16_t
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator that returns the stored 16-bit value of the LocalPortRange. Useful for passing the raw value to APIs that expect a std::uint16_t.

No side effects or error conditions are specified; conversion is read-only and const.

requirements: Arguments must be valid and representable as std::int32_t.

functions.description: Destructor. Cleans up internal resources (e.g., libcurl multi handle, any state associated with added sessions/interceptors).

requirements: Copy assignment is not allowed; callers must not attempt to copy-assign a MultiPerform.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Transfers ownership of internal resources from another MultiPerform instance.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Get
functions.description: Prepares all added sessions to perform HTTP GET requests and executes them, returning a vector of Response objects in session order. Intended for running multiple GETs via the curl multi interface.
requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header (likely returns an empty vector).
Sessions should be properly configured (e.g., URL set) before calling; exact configuration requirements are not specified in the header.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Delete
functions.description: Prepares all added sessions to perform HTTP DELETE requests and executes them, returning their responses.
requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.
Sessions should be configured appropriately for DELETE; details not specified.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Download
functions.description: Prepares all added sessions for a download operation and executes them. Each session must be paired with a corresponding output sink (one argument per session). Supported sink types, as implied by PrepareDownloadSession overloads, are std::ofstream (by non-const lvalue reference) and cpr::WriteCallback (by const reference). Throws std::invalid_argument if the number of arguments does not match the number of sessions.
requirements: The number of provided download arguments must equal the number of sessions previously added via AddSession; otherwise std::invalid_argument is thrown.

Each argument must be of a type accepted by PrepareDownloadSession: either std::ofstream (passed as an lvalue so it can bind to std::ofstream&) or cpr::WriteCallback (or a type convertible to const cpr::WriteCallback&).
Sessions should be suitably configured (e.g., URL set) prior to calling; specifics not documented.
Argument order must correspond to the order of sessions in GetSessions().

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Put
functions.description: Prepares and executes HTTP PUT requests for all added sessions, returning their responses.
requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.
Sessions should be configured appropriately for PUT; details not specified.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Head
functions.description: Prepares and executes HTTP HEAD requests for all added sessions, returning their responses.
requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.
Sessions should be configured appropriately for HEAD; details not specified.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Options
functions.description: Prepares and executes HTTP OPTIONS requests for all added sessions, returning their responses.
requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Patch
functions.description: Prepares and executes HTTP PATCH requests for all added sessions, returning their responses.
requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::Post

requirements: At least zero sessions may be present; behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.

functions.description: Executes the prepared operation for all added sessions and returns their responses. Intended for cases where sessions have been set up previously (e.g., by SetHttpMethod via internal preparation calls or interceptors).
requirements: Intended to be called after appropriate preparation of sessions/method; exact preparation sequence is not specified in the header.
Behavior with no sessions is unspecified in the header.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::PerformDownload
functions.description: Prepares download sinks for the current sessions without altering the current HTTP method, then executes a multi-download request. Each session must have one corresponding sink argument. Throws std::invalid_argument if the number of arguments does not match the number of sessions. Unlike Download(), this function does not call SetHttpMethod; it only binds sinks before executing.
requirements: The number of provided download arguments must equal the number of sessions previously added via AddSession; otherwise std::invalid_argument is thrown.
Each argument must be acceptable to PrepareDownloadSession: std::ofstream& or const cpr::WriteCallback& (or convertible).
Argument order must correspond to the order of sessions in GetSessions().
Sessions should be configured (e.g., URL set) prior to calling; specifics not documented.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::AddSession
functions.description: Adds a cpr::Session to the MultiPerform along with an optional initial HTTP method hint. Sessions are stored internally and later executed by the request methods.

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::RemoveSession

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::GetSessions

functions.name: cpr::MultiPerform::GetSessions

functions.name: cpr::ServerSentEventParser::parse

functions.name: cpr::ThreadPool::Start

functions.name: cpr::ThreadPool::Wait
functions.description: Blocks the caller until a certain pool condition is met (commonly until all tasks complete or the pool reaches an idle state). Returns an int status code; exact semantics and condition are not specified in this header.

functions.name: cpr::ThreadPool::Submit
functions.signature:
template <class Fn, class... Args>
auto cpr::ThreadPool::Submit(Fn&& fn, Args&&... args)
functions.description: Submits a callable and its arguments to be executed asynchronously by the pool and returns a std::future for the callable’s return type. If the pool is STOP, it automatically calls Start(). If no idle threads are available and the current thread count is below max_threads, it attempts to create another worker. The task is packaged via std::packaged_task and queued; workers pick it up and execute it.
requirements: Fn and Args must be invocable as decltype(fn(args...)) and be storable in the task: they are captured by value/move into an internal lambda; therefore, they must be MoveConstructible (CopyConstructible if not movable).
The callable must be safe to run on a worker thread and must not rely on thread-affine state unless externally synchronized.

Exception handling: exceptions thrown by the callable will be stored in the returned future and rethrown on future.get(); packaging/capture-time exceptions will propagate to Submit() and prevent queuing.
Do not pass references that may dangle by the time the task executes; pass by value or ensure referenced objects outlive task execution.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets CPR URL query keys and related small strings used by:
# - Session::SetParameters (keys up to 32, values up to 64)
# - Parameter constructor (keys up to 64, values up to 128)
# - CurlContainer::GetContent/Add (keys up to 16/64, values up to 32/128)
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR will be read repeatedly to build keys/values. We provide a single
# bytes buffer that concatenates multiple interesting strings, each NUL-terminated,
# so the fuzzer stub can slice them as needed. All strings are valid for URL query
# keys/values and cover a wide range of behaviors: ASCII tokens, unicode, percent
# encodings, reserved characters, repeated/empty-ish (but we avoid empty for keys),
# long boundary lengths, and different casings.

# Helper: URL-safe base set and additional reserved/delimiter characters often
# involved in query building and encoding paths.
URL_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.*"
RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n"

# Some unicode sequences that are commonly encountered in URLs/user input
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "café",
    "東京",
    "😀",
    "ñandú",
    "россия",
    "العربية",
]

# Percent-encoded patterns that should remain valid and exercise encode/decode
PERCENTS = [
    "%20", "%2F", "%3F", "%26", "%3D", "%25", "%2B", "%40", "%7E",
]

# Generate an identifier-like key
def gen_key(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Ensure non-empty and start with a letter for server friendliness
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    # Mix of safe chars and a small chance to include reserved to exercise encoding
    pool = URL_SAFE + (RESERVED if rng.random() < 0.35 else "")
    rest_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, max_len - 1))
    s = start + "".join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(rest_len))
    # Occasionally inject percent-encodings or unicode
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(s) < max_len - 3:
        s += rng.choice(PERCENTS)
    if rng.random() < 0.25 and len(s) < max_len - 1:
        s = s[: max(1, len(s) - 1)] + rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        s = s[:max_len]
    return s[:max_len] or "k"

# Generate a value string with broader character coverage
def gen_value(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    choices: List[str] = []
    # Template 1: plain ASCII safe
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
        choices.append("".join(rng.choice(URL_SAFE) for _ in range(n)))
    # Template 2: include reserved characters to trigger encoding
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
        pool = URL_SAFE + RESERVED
        choices.append("".join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n)))
    # Template 3: include whitespace
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
        pool = URL_SAFE + WHITESPACE
        choices.append("".join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(n)))
    # Template 4: unicode heavy
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts = []
        while True:
            if sum(len(p) for p in parts) >= max_len:
                break
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES + [rng.choice(URL_SAFE)]))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                parts.append(rng.choice(PERCENTS))
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                parts.append(rng.choice(WHITESPACE))
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                break
        s = "".join(parts)[:max_len]
        choices.append(s)
    # Template 5: boundary sized strings
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # Prefer producing near-boundary sizes to hit truncation paths
        target = rng.choice([0, max_len//2, max_len-1, max_len])
        if target > 0:
            pool = URL_SAFE + RESERVED
            s = "".join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(target))
        else:
            s = ""
        choices.append(s)
    # Insert some key=value-like values to test encoding of equals and ampersands
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        left = gen_key(rng, max_len//2)
        right = gen_value(rng, max_len//2)
        s = f"{left}={right}"
        choices.append(s[:max_len])

    # Select one deterministically from the built options
    if not choices:
        return ""
    return choices[rng.randrange(len(choices))][:max_len]

# Build a sequence of NUL-terminated strings that FUZZ_PARAM_STR can draw from.
# We include multiple keys and values sized for all observed bounds so all stubs
# can consume useful data from a single buffer.

def build_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Prepare several key/value pairs with specific maximums seen in stubs
    # Keys: 16, 32, 64; Values: 32, 64, 128
    key_sizes = [16, 32, 64]
    val_sizes = [32, 64, 128]

    # Add a small fixed set first with deterministic interesting tokens
    fixed = [
        "page", "limit", "q", "sort", "filter", "X-Custom",
        "token", "session_id", "user", "ÜnicodeKey",
        "name space", "complex/key",
    ]
    for s in fixed:
        parts.append(s.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")

    # Add percent tokens and reserved-only strings to trigger encoding paths
    for p in PERCENTS:
        parts.append(p.encode("ascii") + b"\x00")
    parts.append(RESERVED.encode("ascii") + b"\x00")

    # Now randomized keys/values across sizes
    for _ in range(20):
        k = gen_key(rng, rng.choice(key_sizes))
        parts.append(k.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
        v = gen_value(rng, rng.choice(val_sizes))
        parts.append(v.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")

    # Boundary-focused: exact max size tokens
    for ks in key_sizes:
        k = gen_key(rng, ks)
        parts.append(k.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")
    for vs in val_sizes:
        v = gen_value(rng, vs)
        parts.append(v.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure we respect the 4096-byte limit; if too large, truncate at last NUL
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        trunc = blob[:4096]
        last_nul = trunc.rfind(b"\x00")
        if last_nul == -1:
            # fallback: force a terminator at end
            trunc = trunc[:-1] + b"\x00"
        else:
            trunc = trunc[: last_nul + 1]
        blob = trunc
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_buffer(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: URL query value (string used as value for a query parameter)
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to build keys and values for:
# - cpr::Session::SetParameters (two key/value pairs)
# - cpr::Parameter ctor
# - CurlContainer Parameters/Payload Add/GetContent
# Additionally, urlEncode/urlDecode are exercised over arbitrary strings.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a bytes buffer that, when split by the fuzzing harness to fill FUZZ_PARAM_STR(),
#   yields a diverse set of short-to-medium strings containing:
#   * URL-safe tokens
#   * Characters requiring percent-encoding (space, +, %, #, &, =, ?, /, \n, \r, \t)
#   * UTF-8 multibyte sequences (e.g., emoji, CJK)
#   * Boundary-length strings within caps seen in stubs (keys <= 64, values <= 128)
#   * Empty and very short strings
#   * Pre-encoded sequences (%HH) to exercise decode
# - Use a simple TLV-like framing: for each string, emit: [len_hi][len_lo][payload]
#   where length is 0..255 (we cap segment length to 255 to keep total <= 4096).
#   Many fuzzers feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR by consuming framed segments from the input.
# - Keep total size <= 4096.
# - Deterministic randomness with provided seed.

URL_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
# Characters often needing encoding or significant in URLs
URL_SPECIALS = " %+#&=?/\n\r\t\0" + "!$'()*,:;@[]{}<>\"\\|^`"
# Some interesting percent-encoded sequences (valid and edge cases)
PCT_SEQS = [
    "%20", "%2F", "%3F", "%23", "%25", "%2B", "%26", "%3D",
    "%00", "%7E", "%41", "%7f", "%c3", "%C3%A9", "%F0%9F%98%80"
]
# Some Unicode samples
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "é", "ñ", "中", "文", "测试", "🙂", "😀", "🚀", "💡", "π", "✓", "Δ",
]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: str, k: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(seq) for _ in range(k))


def _make_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Keys typically avoid spaces; include a few specials but keep readable
    base_len = rng.randint(1, 24)
    s = _rand_choice(rng, URL_SAFE, base_len)
    # Occasionally add a special char (not '=' or '&' at ends to keep servers happy)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        insert_pos = rng.randint(0, len(s))
        ch = rng.choice("-_" + string.digits + "@.:" + "_" + " ")
        s = s[:insert_pos] + ch + s[insert_pos:]
    # Ensure non-empty and <= 64 (stub truncates anyway)
    return s[:64] if s else "k"


def _make_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a mix of URL-safe, specials, percent-encoded, and unicode
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Start with some safe core
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, URL_SAFE, rng.randint(0, 16)))
    # Optionally add unicode
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
    # Add specials burst
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        specials = ''.join(rng.choice(URL_SPECIALS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
        parts.append(specials)
    # Add percent-encoded sequences
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(PCT_SEQS))
    # Add more safe tail
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, URL_SAFE, rng.randint(0, 32)))
    # Occasionally start with '?' or '&' to exercise edge in payload building
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.insert(0, rng.choice(["?", "&"]))
    # Occasionally include repeated '%' to stress encoder
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append("%" * rng.randint(1, 3))
    val = ''.join(parts)
    # Ensure length reasonable; stubs cap values at 128 for some paths
    if len(val) == 0:
        val = "v"
    return val[:200]


def _make_encoded_blob(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a string that is already percent-encoded for urlDecode test
    raw_len = rng.randint(4, 24)
    raw = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(raw_len))
    hexchars = "0123456789ABCDEF"
    out = []
    for i, b in enumerate(raw):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            out.append('%')
            out.append(hexchars[(b >> 4) & 0xF])
            out.append(hexchars[b & 0xF])
        else:
            ch = chr(b)
            # Keep printable non-space occasionally, else encode
            if 32 <= b < 127 and ch not in "%#&=?/ ":
                out.append(ch)
            else:
                out.append('%')
                out.append(hexchars[(b >> 4) & 0xF])
                out.append(hexchars[b & 0xF])
    return ''.join(out)


def _frame(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # 2-byte length prefix per string (big-endian), payload in UTF-8
    bufs: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        if len(b) > 65535:
            b = b[:65535]
        ln = len(b)
        seg = bytes([(ln >> 8) & 0xFF, ln & 0xFF]) + b
        if total + len(seg) > 4096:
            break
        bufs.append(seg)
        total += len(seg)
    return b''.join(bufs)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings: List[str] = []

    # Provide a mix of keys/values first (for SetParameters, Parameter, Add)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        strings.append(_make_key(rng))
        strings.append(_make_value(rng))

    # Add some standalone values to exercise urlEncode/urlDecode paths
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.25:
            strings.append(_make_encoded_blob(rng))
        elif choice < 0.5:
            # Heavier on specials
            strings.append(_make_value(rng))
        elif choice < 0.75:
            # Pure URL-safe
            strings.append(_rand_choice(rng, URL_SAFE, rng.randint(0, 40)))
        else:
            # Unicode heavy
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
            # Mix with a few specials
            s += ''.join(rng.choice(URL_SPECIALS) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))
            strings.append(s)

    # Include some edge cases: empty, single-char, long near caps
    strings.extend([
        "",  # empty
        rng.choice(string.ascii_letters),
        _rand_choice(rng, URL_SAFE + URL_SPECIALS, 64),  # ~key cap
        _rand_choice(rng, URL_SAFE + URL_SPECIALS, 128), # ~value common cap
    ])

    # Frame into length-prefixed segments to help the harness split FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    return _frame(strings)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: HTTP header name (and related header values/status lines in stubs)
# The fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() extensively to build:
# - Header names (must avoid control chars and ':', length <= 32)
# - Header values (arbitrary text but avoid CR/LF inside a single line, length <= 128)
# - Cookie names/values (similar constraints, names <= 32, values <= 64)
# - HTTP status reason phrase (no CR/LF)
# - Full HTTP header blocks for parseHeader (must include: status line, headers, CRLF terminator)
# - headerUserFunction expects a single well-formed header line with CRLF
#
# Our buffer will contain multiple newline-delimited tokens so the harness can
# consume them via FUZZ_PARAM_STR()/FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned) in order. We craft a
# sequence covering all stubs with valid data and interesting variations.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

TOKEN_SEP = "\n"  # Line separator for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls

# Character sets
TOKEN_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_."  # safe for header names
VALUE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
# Remove CR/LF and colon from values that must be a single line; we sanitize later where needed
VALUE_CHARS = VALUE_CHARS.replace("\n", "").replace("\r", "")


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, chars: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


def make_header_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ensure it starts with an alpha to be conservative
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    rest = rand_choice(rng, TOKEN_CHARS, 0, 31)
    return (start + rest)[:32]


def make_header_value(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 128) -> str:
    # Single-line value, avoid CR/LF
    val = rand_choice(rng, VALUE_CHARS, 0, max_len)
    # trim trailing spaces occasionally
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        val = val.rstrip()
    return val[:max_len]


def make_cookie_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Cookie token name similar constraints as header name
    return make_header_name(rng)[:32]


def make_cookie_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Values can include wider punctuation but not CR/LF
    return make_header_value(rng, 64)


def make_reason_phrase(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Human-like reasons without CR/LF
    choices = [
        "OK", "Created", "Accepted", "No Content", "Moved Permanently", "Found",
        "See Other", "Not Modified", "Bad Request", "Unauthorized", "Forbidden",
        "Not Found", "Method Not Allowed", "Conflict", "Gone", "Length Required",
        "Precondition Failed", "Payload Too Large", "URI Too Long", "Unsupported Media Type",
        "Too Many Requests", "Internal Server Error", "Not Implemented", "Bad Gateway",
        "Service Unavailable", "Gateway Timeout"
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    # Or synthesize
    return make_header_value(rng, 40)


def make_status_code(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Valid HTTP status 100..599
    return rng.randint(100, 599)


def build_http_header_block(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a minimal but valid header block for cpr::util::parseHeader
    status = make_status_code(rng)
    reason = make_reason_phrase(rng)
    lines: List[str] = []
    lines.append(f"HTTP/1.1 {status} {reason}\r\n")
    # At least one header
    h1 = f"{make_header_name(rng)}: {make_header_value(rng)}\r\n"
    lines.append(h1)
    # Optionally add a second header
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        h2 = f"{make_header_name(rng)}: {make_header_value(rng)}\r\n"
        lines.append(h2)
    # Terminating CRLF
    lines.append("\r\n")
    return ''.join(lines)


def build_single_header_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For headerUserFunction: a single header line terminated with CRLF
    return f"{make_header_name(rng)}: {make_header_value(rng)}\r\n"


def assemble_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens: List[str] = []

    # For Session::SetHeader: hk1, hv1, hk2, hv2
    tokens.append(make_header_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))

    # For Session::UpdateHeader: hk, hv
    tokens.append(make_header_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))

    # For Session::GetHeader mutation: hk, hv
    tokens.append(make_header_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))

    # For SetCookies: cn1, cv1, cn2, cv2
    tokens.append(make_cookie_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_cookie_value(rng))
    tokens.append(make_cookie_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_cookie_value(rng))

    # For CaseInsensitiveCompare: two arbitrary strings (we choose header-like to avoid embedded NULs)
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))

    # For parseHeader: reason, hname, hval, h2name, h2val; plus additional optional pulls
    # Although the stub sanitizes, we still provide clean inputs.
    tokens.append(make_reason_phrase(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_name(rng))
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))

    # Additional pulls for flags (FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)) are numeric, not from our string stream.

    # For headerUserFunction: a base line payload; stub will add CRLF if missing, but we make a proper header-ish token
    tokens.append(make_header_value(rng))

    # Also embed fully formed header blocks and single lines as separate tokens for consumers
    # that might pass filenames or larger blobs into FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
    tokens.append(build_http_header_block(rng))
    tokens.append(build_single_header_line(rng))

    # Ensure tokens are not empty (FUZZ_PARAM_STR might provide empty, but stubs guard empties only for names)
    tokens = [t if t else "X" for t in tokens]
    return tokens


def clamp_bytes(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b[:MAX_TOTAL]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    tokens = assemble_tokens(rng)

    # Join tokens with newline separator so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR() call can consume one token.
    # Keep total size under limit.
    payload = TOKEN_SEP.join(tokens)

    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        prefix = f"#seed={seed}-{rng.randint(0, 1<<16)}\n"
        payload = prefix + payload

    data = payload.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    return clamp_bytes(data)

import string
from typing import List

# Data type: password string
# Goal: Generate interesting but valid password strings that exercise auth-related code paths.
# Constraints observed in stubs:
# - Passwords are truncated to <= 64 bytes in several stubs.
# - They may be used in URL encoding and secure storage; include characters that need encoding.
# - They may be combined with different auth modes and proxies; include edge cases and diverse char classes.
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects arbitrary byte-like content; we return UTF-8 bytes.
# Size limit: keep <= 4096 bytes (we keep <= 64 to match truncation in stubs).

MAX_LEN = 64

# Character groups to exercise encoding/escaping and edge cases
ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(32, 127))
LOWER = string.ascii_lowercase
UPPER = string.ascii_uppercase
DIGITS = string.digits
WHITESPACE = ' \t\n\r\v\f'
PUNCT_SIMPLE = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?"  # common punctuation
URL_RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
URL_UNSAFE = "%<>{}|\\^`"  # percent and others
QUOTES = "'\"``"
UNICODE_SETS = [
    # Some non-ASCII to test UTF-8 handling/encoding
    "äöüÄÖÜß€£¥©®™✓★❄",           # Latin-1 + symbols
    "你好世界こんにちは안녕하세요",   # CJK
    "🙂🙃😉😍🤖👾🐍🚀",            # emoji
]

COMMON_PASSWORDS = [
    "",  # empty
    " ",
    "password",
    "Password",
    "P@ssw0rd",
    "letmein",
    "admin",
    "123456",
    "1234567890",
    "qwerty",
    "correcthorsebatterystaple",
]

EDGE_CASES = [
    "%", "%%", "%00", "%20",  # percent/URL-encoding triggers
    "\\", "\\\\",           # backslashes
    "\n", "\r\n",               # newlines
    ":", "@", ":@",             # auth delimiter characters
    "\0",                          # literal NUL won’t survive in Python string -> we simulate via escaped text
]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _random_len(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(min_len, max_len)


def _mix_groups(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Build a password containing a mix of classes to exercise encoding and storage
    groups = [LOWER, UPPER, DIGITS, PUNCT_SIMPLE, URL_RESERVED, URL_UNSAFE]
    parts = []
    # Ensure at least one from several groups when length permits
    for g in groups:
        if len(parts) >= target_len:
            break
        parts.append(rng.choice(g))
    # Optionally add some unicode
    if target_len > len(parts) and rng.random() < 0.5:
        uni = _rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SETS)
        parts.append(rng.choice(uni))
    # Fill remaining with a combined pool
    pool = ''.join(groups) + ''.join(UNICODE_SETS)
    while len(parts) < target_len:
        ch = rng.choice(pool)
        parts.append(ch)
    rng.shuffle(parts)
    return ''.join(parts)


def _repeat_pattern(rng: random.Random, base: str, target_len: int) -> str:
    if not base:
        base = "a"
    s = (base * (target_len // len(base) + 1))[:target_len]
    return s


def _make_interesting_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    candidates = []
    # Include common passwords and edge cases
    candidates.extend(COMMON_PASSWORDS)
    candidates.extend(EDGE_CASES)

    # Boundary lengths
    for L in [1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64]:
        candidates.append(_mix_groups(rng, L))
        candidates.append(_repeat_pattern(rng, "A%", L))
        candidates.append(_repeat_pattern(rng, "\t\n", L))

    # URL-sensitive compositions
    candidates.append("user:pass@host")
    candidates.append("p@ss:word")
    candidates.append("col:on;semi;")
    candidates.append("enc%2Fslash%3Fq%3D1")

    # High-unicode heavy
    uni = ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SETS) for _ in range(3))
    candidates.append(uni[:MAX_LEN])

    # Whitespace heavy
    candidates.append(_repeat_pattern(rng, WHITESPACE, 32))

    # JSON-like and shell-like to test escaping in logs
    candidates.append('{"key":"val"}')
    candidates.append("$(whoami); echo")

    # Long mixed string at limit
    candidates.append(_mix_groups(rng, MAX_LEN))

    return candidates


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy
    strategy = rng.random()
    if strategy < 0.5:
        # Pick from curated candidates
        cands = _make_interesting_candidates(rng)
        value = rng.choice(cands)
    else:
        # Construct a fresh random one
        length = _random_len(rng, 0, MAX_LEN)
        # 50% chance to be a repeated pattern, else mixed groups
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            base_choices = ["%", "A%", "\t\n", " :@", "..//", "💥", "😊", "\r\n"]
            value = _repeat_pattern(rng, rng.choice(base_choices), length)
        else:
            value = _mix_groups(rng, length)

    # Ensure max length constraint
    if len(value) > MAX_LEN:
        value = value[:MAX_LEN]

    # Encode to bytes. Use UTF-8 to allow unicode; replace errors to stay valid bytes always
    return value.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')

from typing import List

# Data type: form field name (used as keys in application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart parts)
# Goals for interesting, valid values:
# - Non-empty ASCII tokens commonly accepted in form encodings
# - Cover typical characters: letters, digits, underscore, dash, dot
# - Include bracket notation often used for arrays/objects: name[], user[name]
# - Include dotted nested names: user.address.street
# - Include repeated keys and similar prefixes to tickle map/set logic
# - Keep size within fuzzer stub caps (<= 32 chars for keys)
# - Provide variation while remaining valid

MAX_KEY_LEN = 32

_simple_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-."
_bracket_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.[]"

_common_keys = [
    "a",
    "b",
    "q",
    "id",
    "key",
    "name",
    "value",
    "token",
    "session",
    "user",
    "email",
    "password",
    "search",
    "query",
    "page",
    "limit",
    "offset",
    "sort",
    "filter",
    "csrf_token",
    "auth[username]",
    "auth[password]",
    "user[name]",
    "user[email]",
    "items[]",
    "tags[]",
    "user.address.street",
    "user.address.zip",
    "meta.version",
    "data[items][][id]",
]


def _rand_str(rng: random.Random, length: int, alphabet: str) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def _make_simple_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Start with a letter to be conservative for some parsers
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    rest_len = rng.randint(0, MAX_KEY_LEN - 1)
    rest = _rand_str(rng, rest_len, _simple_chars)
    return (first + rest)[:MAX_KEY_LEN]


def _make_bracket_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build patterns like: base, base[], base[sub], base[sub][idx]
    base = _make_simple_key(rng)
    # Trim base to leave room for brackets
    base = base[: max(1, MAX_KEY_LEN - 10)]
    forms: List[str] = []
    # []
    forms.append(f"{base}[]")
    # [word]
    sub = _make_simple_key(rng)
    forms.append(f"{base}[{sub[:8]}]")
    # [word][num]
    num = str(rng.randint(0, 999))
    forms.append(f"{base}[{sub[:6]}][{num}]")
    # nested triple
    sub2 = _make_simple_key(rng)
    forms.append(f"{base}[{sub[:4]}][{sub2[:4]}]")
    key = rng.choice(forms)
    return key[:MAX_KEY_LEN]


def _make_dotted_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    remaining = MAX_KEY_LEN
    n_parts = rng.randint(2, 4)
    for i in range(n_parts):
        # ensure at least 1 char per remaining part plus dots
        left = n_parts - i
        max_part = max(1, remaining - (left - 1) - (left - 1))
        plen = rng.randint(1, min(10, max_part))
        seg = _rand_str(rng, plen, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_")
        parts.append(seg)
        remaining -= len(seg)
        if i != n_parts - 1:
            remaining -= 1
    key = '.'.join(parts)
    return key[:MAX_KEY_LEN]


def _make_prefixed_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = rng.choice(["x_", "p_", "custom_", "opt_", "hdr_"])
    core = _make_simple_key(rng)
    return (prefix + core)[:MAX_KEY_LEN]


def _choose_common_or_generated(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        return rng.choice(_common_keys)[:MAX_KEY_LEN]
    kind = rng.random()
    if kind < 0.40:
        return _make_simple_key(rng)
    elif kind < 0.70:
        return _make_bracket_key(rng)
    elif kind < 0.90:
        return _make_dotted_key(rng)
    else:
        return _make_prefixed_key(rng)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce a small corpus batch to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations.
    # The fuzz stubs often call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times for keys
    # and will clamp to <= 32 chars; we ensure non-empty and varied.
    n = rng.randint(2, 8)
    keys = []
    for _ in range(n):
        k = _choose_common_or_generated(rng)
        if not k:
            k = "a"
        if len(k) > MAX_KEY_LEN:
            k = k[:MAX_KEY_LEN]
        keys.append(k)

    # Add a few crafted combinations to exercise duplicates and similar prefixes
    if rng.random() < 0.8 and keys:
        base = keys[0].split('[')[0].split('.')[0]
        variants = [
            base,
            f"{base}[]",
            f"{base}[0]",
            f"{base}[name]",
            f"{base}.id",
        ]
        for v in variants:
            if len(v) <= MAX_KEY_LEN:
                keys.append(v)

    # Join with newlines so that a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR read can consume
    # one line at a time in the harness environment that splits inputs.
    # If the harness reads raw bytes, it will still provide diverse substrings.
    payload = "\n".join(keys)
    # Ensure total size under 4096 bytes
    b = payload.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: form field value (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
# We generate percent-encoded-safe strings and also include interesting characters
# that are valid when properly encoded by the library (cpr will urlencode when needed).
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR provides raw bytes; here we return bytes for the fuzzer to use as-is.

SAFE_UNRESERVED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"
# Characters that often trigger different code paths when present in form values
INTERESTING = [
    " ", "\t", "\n", "\r", "+", "%", "&", "=", ":", ";", ",", "/", "?",
    "#", "[", "]", "(", ")", "'", '"', "*"
]

# Some common Unicode snippets that are valid in UTF-8 and often appear in real-world inputs
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    " café", "∆", "✓", "💡", "–", "—", "€", "ñ", "ø", "中", "文", "こんにちは"
]

COMMON_VALUES = [
    "",  # empty value valid in form encoding
    "0", "1", "true", "false", "null",
    "a", "b", "test", "value", "example",
    "email@example.com", "user_name", "first+last",
    "a=b&c=d",  # contains separators to exercise encoding paths
    "%done",     # percent sign
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _gen_unreserved(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_UNRESERVED) for _ in range(length))

def _gen_mixed(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Build from unreserved plus interesting tokens, occasionally insert unicode snippets
    out: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < length:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            out.append(rng.choice(SAFE_UNRESERVED))
            i += 1
        elif choice < 0.9 and length - i >= 1:
            out.append(_rand_choice(rng, INTERESTING))
            i += 1
        else:
            snippet = _rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SNIPPETS)
            # ensure not to exceed target length too much; if too big, fallback to single char
            if i + len(snippet) <= length:
                out.append(snippet)
                i += len(snippet)
            else:
                out.append(rng.choice(SAFE_UNRESERVED))
                i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

def _gen_form_value(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a strategy to produce variety while remaining valid
    strategy = rng.randrange(6)
    if strategy == 0:
        # Common literals
        s = _rand_choice(rng, COMMON_VALUES)
    elif strategy == 1:
        # Pure unreserved of moderate length
        n = rng.randint(1, 64)
        s = _gen_unreserved(rng, n)
    elif strategy == 2:
        # Mixed with separators to exercise encoding
        n = rng.randint(1, 96)
        s = _gen_mixed(rng, n)
    elif strategy == 3:
        # Key/value-like content, but as a single value
        left = _gen_mixed(rng, rng.randint(1, 16))
        right = _gen_mixed(rng, rng.randint(0, 24))
        s = f"{left}={right}"
    elif strategy == 4:
        # Ampersand-separated list inside value
        parts = [
            _gen_mixed(rng, rng.randint(0, 12))
            for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))
        ]
        s = "&".join(parts)
    else:
        # Include percent-escape-like patterns; still valid text prior to encoding
        base = _gen_mixed(rng, rng.randint(1, 48))
        # Insert a few %XX patterns
        hexpairs = [
            f"%{rng.choice('0123456789ABCDEF')}{rng.choice('0123456789ABCDEF')}"
            for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))
        ]
        insert_positions = sorted({rng.randrange(len(base)+1) for _ in range(len(hexpairs))})
        cur = 0
        chunks: List[str] = []
        for pos, hx in zip(insert_positions, hexpairs):
            chunks.append(base[cur:pos])
            chunks.append(hx)
            cur = pos
        chunks.append(base[cur:])
        s = ''.join(chunks)

    # Bound total size to 4096 bytes when encoded as UTF-8
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce between 1 and 4 concatenated form values separated by newlines to
    # seed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls with diverse yet valid values.
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    vals = [_gen_form_value(rng) for _ in range(count)]
    # Separate with newline so individual FUZZ_PARAM_STR() extractions can split as needed by the harness.
    # The fuzzer framework generally treats the entire buffer as a blob; using delimiters helps variety.
    return b"\n".join(vals)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path
# We want to generate valid, interesting paths for uses such as:
# - Unix domain socket path (absolute, prefixed with "/", length <= 255 preferred)
# - Certificate/key/CRL/CA paths (may be absolute or relative; with various extensions)
# - Filenames for temporary buffers
# Fuzzer stubs cap many strings (e.g., 128 chars) and sometimes coerce to absolute.
# We'll generate a mix of absolute/relative POSIX-like paths, including edge cases:
# - Deep nested directories
# - Hidden files, dot and dotdot segments
# - Various extensions: .pem, .der, .crt, .key, .pem.enc
# - Paths with spaces and special but valid characters
# - Very short and near-limit lengths
# - Common system-like paths under /etc/ssl, /tmp, /var/run, etc.
# Note: We only return bytes; the fuzzing framework will distribute into FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.

MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 4096

_EXTS = ["", ".pem", ".crt", ".der", ".key", ".pem.enc", ".txt"]
_COMPONENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_#@%+"  # safe filename chars
_WS_CHARS = " "  # allow spaces occasionally
_SPECIAL_DIRS = [".", "..", ".hidden", "config", "certs", "keys", "crl", "ca", "sockets", "tmp"]
_ROOTS = [
    "/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/var/run", "/run", "/etc", "/etc/ssl", "/usr/local/share/ca-certificates",
    "/home/user", "/opt/app", "/srv", "/dev/shm"
]

_REL_ROOTS = [
    "./", "../", "certs/", "keys/", "crl/", "ca/", "sockets/", "build/", "data/", "./.cache/"
]

_SOCKET_BASENAMES = ["cpr.sock", "app.sock", "api.socket", "unix.d", "sock", ".hidden.sock"]
_CERT_BASENAMES = [
    "cert", "client", "server", "bundle", "chain", "ca-bundle", "key", "private", "public", "pkey"
]


def _rand(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16, allow_ws=True):
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = _COMPONENT_CHARS + (_WS_CHARS if allow_ws and rng.random() < 0.2 else "")
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces to keep paths sane
    if length == 1:
        return rng.choice(chars.replace(" ", "") or _COMPONENT_CHARS)
    s = "".join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    s = s.strip() or "x"
    return s


def _build_posix_path(rng: random.Random, absolute: bool, depth_range=(1, 6), purpose: str = "generic") -> str:
    depth = rng.randint(*depth_range)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Seed with special dirs occasionally
    for _ in range(depth):
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append(_rand(rng, _SPECIAL_DIRS))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_component(rng))

    # Choose base name depending on purpose
    if purpose == "socket":
        base = _rand(rng, _SOCKET_BASENAMES)
    elif purpose == "certlike":
        base = _rand(rng, _CERT_BASENAMES)
        base += _rand(rng, _EXTS)
    else:
        base = _rand_component(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            base += _rand(rng, _EXTS)

    parts.append(base)

    # Join with a root
    if absolute:
        root = _rand(rng, _ROOTS)
        path = root.rstrip("/") + "/" + "/".join(p.strip("/") for p in parts if p)
    else:
        root = _rand(rng, _REL_ROOTS)
        path = root + "/".join(p.strip("/") for p in parts if p)

    # Normalize duplicate slashes lightly
    path = path.replace("//", "/")

    # Length constraints for Unix socket path suggest <=255; clamp occasionally
    if purpose == "socket" and len(path) > 255:
        # Keep basename and trim intermediate dirs
        head, _, tail = path.rpartition("/")
        tail = tail[:60] or "sock"
        path = head[: max(1, 240 - len(tail))].rstrip("/") + "/" + tail

    # General cap to keep individual entries modest
    if len(path) > 1024:
        path = path[:1024]

    return path


def _mix_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths: List[str] = []

    # Ensure at least one valid absolute Unix socket-like path
    paths.append(_build_posix_path(rng, absolute=True, depth_range=(1, 4), purpose="socket"))

    # A few certificate-like absolute paths
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        paths.append(_build_posix_path(rng, absolute=True, depth_range=(1, 5), purpose="certlike"))

    # Relative paths
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        paths.append(_build_posix_path(rng, absolute=False, depth_range=(1, 4), purpose="generic"))

    # Edge cases
    paths.append("/tmp/" + _rand(rng, _SOCKET_BASENAMES))
    paths.append("/etc/ssl/certs/" + _rand(rng, _CERT_BASENAMES) + _rand(rng, [".pem", ".crt"]))
    paths.append("/var/run/" + _rand(rng, _SOCKET_BASENAMES))

    # Near 255-char socket path: create a deep path with controlled length
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        base = "/var/run/"
        target_len = rng.randint(200, 255)
        # Build repeated components to reach target
        comp = "a" * 10
        s = base
        while len(s) + len(comp) + 1 < target_len:
            s += comp + "/"
        s += _rand(rng, _SOCKET_BASENAMES)
        paths.append(s[:255])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for p in paths:
        if p not in seen:
            seen.add(p)
            uniq.append(p)
    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a corpus of paths
    paths = _mix_paths(rng)

    # Join them with NUL separators so a consumer can split or pick as needed.
    # Many fuzz harnesses read a single blob and reuse it for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
    blob = ("\0").join(paths)
    data = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not data:
        data = b"/tmp/cpr.sock"

    # Cap to framework maximum
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL_BYTES]

    return data
